messages:
acme-prod: Hey team — since yesterday ~14:00 UTC our assistant started giving inconsistent answers for the same prompt. Two requests with identical prompt return different facts. Happening across users and runs, not just one session. Example below with request IDs and responses. Can you help?

acme-prod: Request A: request_id=01FZ8ABC; prompt="What is AcmeCorp's refund policy?" -> model: rwd-llama-13b-v2 -> "Refunds processed within 30 days..."

acme-prod: Request B: request_id=01FZ8ABD; prompt="What is AcmeCorp's refund policy?" -> model: rwd-llama-13b-compat -> "We no longer offer refunds after purchase..."  

acme-prod: Both requests made within 3s of each other from same client and API key. No retries on our side. This started after the last platform update.

anne (Support): Thanks — that looks bad, sorry for the disruption. Can you paste the raw API responses (headers + body) for both requests? Also which region and client api_key? We need to confirm model routing metadata.

acme-prod: Pasted (redacted):

``
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: 01FZ8ABC
x-model-id: rwd-llama-13b-v2
{"output":"Refunds processed within 30 days...","usage":{...}}
```

``
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-request-id: 01FZ8ABD
x-model-id: rwd-llama-13b-compat
{"output":"We no longer offer refunds after purchase...","usage":{...}}
```

jin (SRE): @anne looks like routing returned two different model variants. I just pulled the routing logs for that api_key and see alternating routes between rwd-llama-13b-v2 and rwd-llama-13b-compat around that time. We recently lowered the compatibility-fallback threshold in the rollout for latency-sensitive routes; it's possible some requests are being routed to the compat variant when capacity is constrained. :eyes: 

sam (Eng-ML): Adding context — rwd-llama-13b-compat is a smaller-quantized variant we expose as a fallback. It was meant to be functionally equivalent for typical prompts, but we discovered a tokenizer patch and a prompt-prepend difference in the compat build that can change small factual output (especially for short, ambiguous prompts). This explains the divergence.

anne (Support): Important: customer is seeing real business impact. Short-term mitigation: please ask customer to pin model_version in the request (model_version: "rwd-llama-13b-v2") or set routing.strict=true. Share sample curl:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "prompt": "What is AcmeCorp\'s refund policy?",
    "model": "rwd-llama-13b-v2",
    "routing": {"strict": true}
  }'
```

acme-prod: Ok we'll pin as a temporary measure. Can you also confirm this is a rollout change and what the timeline is for a fix? We need assurance this won't happen in production traffic.

jin (SRE): Confirmed rollout change. I will roll back the lowered fallback threshold for the affected region and add a canary exclusion for API keys with >1k monthly calls. Rolling back now and will monitor. :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: canary rollback initiated for routing-policy v1.9.4 -> v1.9.3 by jin (SRE)

sam (Eng-ML): Long-term fix: we'll align tokenizer and prompt normalization across compat variants, and add an automated regression test in the model onboarding pipeline that checks for semantic drift on a curated prompt suite. ETA: patch and rollout in 5 business days.

anne (Support): Thanks all. @acme-prod once you confirm pinning resolves the problem on your end we'll keep you updated on rollback progress and the eng plan. Apologies for the break — we'll prioritize a postmortem and a customer-facing summary.

acme-prod: Pinning stopped the divergence in our quick smoke tests. Appreciate the quick response. Please keep us posted on the rollback and the regression test plan. :pray: 

anne (Support): Will do — creating an incident ticket and will attach logs. Threading internal follow-ups to #incidents and #eng-runtime. Closing here for now but will reopen if anything recurs. Thanks everyone.
